title: Deseasonalized filing-lag conditioning (own_z): norm-relative lateness as a firm-state friction signal on the death-inclusive cohort (Givoly-Palmon / Chambers-Penman late-filer lineage)
mechanism: WHO is the constrained actor: the filer's own reporting machinery — management and its accounting/audit chain — faces a cost of producing and releasing each period's numbers, and that cost spikes exactly when the period contains bad news (loss emergence, impairment triage, control weaknesses, accounting-function turnover) or when the firm is sliding toward distress (Givoly-Palmon 1982; Trueman 1990; Begley-Fischer 1998). The counterparty is the attention-constrained investor who conditions on THAT a filing happened but not on WHEN it happened relative to the filer's own seasonal habit, so the lateness component of the event is priced slowly if at all. WHY the effect exists: statutory deadlines and calendar load are common to all filers, but the DEVIATION of a filer's lag from its own seasonal norm is the costly, firm-period-specific component — producing a filing materially later than one's own habit requires burying worse news, a degraded reporting capability, or distress-driven staff/control failure, each of which predicts weaker subsequent fundamentals that flow into returns over the following quarter. The literature documents the crude version (late announcers underperform; Chambers-Penman 1984; Kross-Schroeder 1984) and documents that release timing is a persistent firm policy (Sengupta 2004; Bagnoli-Kross-Watts 2002) — persistence is exactly what makes an own-history norm the right conditioner: it subtracts the filer's baseline speed and isolates the per-period shock. WHAT observable measures it: own_z from the frozen P0 timing layer (first_lag_days of the filer-period minus the filer's own prior-only seasonal median, scaled by 1.4826*MAD; min_hist_own 4; evidence stamp = first_avail; clock V10-T2), read as the most recent computable own_z within the 800-day bound at each decision gate; coverage is deep on both legs (own_z computable: 4,095,660 groups pooled; ALIVE_EVIDENCED 1,672,712 / DEAD_EVIDENCED 2,422,948 — the dead leg, which populates the late tail and carries its delisting returns in the price series, is MORE heavily funded than the alive leg). WHEN it must fail: (i) if the raw un-normalized lag control (V10-T1) reproduces the anchor at >= 0.5x alpha ratio same-sign, the information is generic delay — a size/complexity/calendar-load proxy and the known crude anomaly — not norm-relative state, and the family dies; (ii) if pooled D2 Spearman |rho| > 0.20 vs any of the nine veto entries (the live risk is 63-session prior return and cash-level, since late filers skew small and weakened), the proposal is INELIGIBLE before selection; (iii) if > 90% of the short-leg expectancy comes from names whose final bar falls within 21 sessions of entry, the mechanism is terminal death-event mechanics, not timeliness, and the family is not promotable as a timeliness mechanism; (iv) any inherited Stage-A gate failure per the ex-ante margins below. WHICH control kills the convenient explanation: the raw first_lag_days control — same universe, same books, same direction, ZERO normalization — is exactly 'the late-filer anomaly in its crudest published form'; if that reproduces the anchor, every convenient explanation (generic delay, small-cap quality drag, filing-season load) survives and the deseasonalized-state claim is dead.
falsifiable_prediction: Directional and falsifiable: within-sector terciles of exposure = -own_z predict relative returns over the inherited 21-session decision window — the earliest-vs-own-norm tercile outperforms the latest-vs-own-norm tercile in at least 2 of 3 folds after base band costs, with (a) long-short expectancy > 0, (b) position PF >= 1.10, (c) the SHORT leg (latest vs own norm) carrying the majority of the spread: short-leg expectancy <= -0.5 x long-leg expectancy — the documented direction of the anomaly is a late-filer penalty, not a prompt-filer quality premium (Chambers-Penman 1984; Kross-Schroeder 1984); if the entire spread is the long leg, the family is recorded as prompt-filer-quality, mechanism-mistitled, and rejected, (d) risk-matched excess vs SPY positive in >= 2 folds and overall alpha > 0, (e) the raw-lag control (V10-T1, no normalization) NOT reproducing the anchor: |control alpha| < 0.5x anchor alpha AND the control never outperforming the anchor in the anchor's direction (a control that outperforms a negative anchor falsifies the family — inherited causal-control rule), (f) the cohort_z neighbour (V10-T3) supporting same sign — if the neighbour flips sign while the anchor passes, the effect is filer-idiosyncratic only and the terminal records the cohort-relative frame as wrong, (g) anchor-vs-control Spearman rho < 0.95 measured pre-selection on the decision grid (they share the lag variable, so nonzero correlation is expected — the V9 precedent of declared-nonzero-but-not-identical — rank-identity is forbidden), and (h) pooled Spearman |rho| <= 0.20 vs all nine veto entries measured at D2 pre-selection. If any of (a)-(h) fails, the family is rejected and deseasonalized filing-lag conditioning is declared untradable on this cohort at these costs; every failure mode is a successful research outcome.

entry_exit_fills.entry: signals computed on session t data under the PIT gate (00:00 UTC t); fills at the next global session close; no same-session fill (inherited fill clock)
entry_exit_fills.fill_check_preregistered: a fill references only names with a bar at the fill session; a missing bar means the order does not exist — no silent substitute pricing (p3 dead-name book semantics)
entry_exit_fills.exit_preregistered: a held name whose series ends is exited at its LAST recorded close on its final session; the delisting return is carried by the price series itself — no synthetic penalty, no synthetic continuation
entry_exit_fills.no_survivorship_resubstitution: a dead name is never replaced by a successor entity's series; books re-form only at decision sessions from the surviving-eligible set
entry_exit_fills.weights: inherited: equal-weight within legs, 1/n_active allocation per sector, 0.5 long / 0.5 short per active sector, CASH absorbs residual; min 1 non-CASH leg per decision, min 30 scored decisions overall, min 5 scored decisions per fold
entry_exit_fills.hysteresis: one-tercile retention on book membership between decisions (inherited runner rule) to hold turnover inside the frozen 6.0x/yr ceiling
entry_exit_fills.kernel_change_note: exit-at-last-close semantics already frozen by V9 (resolve_exit_band_bps charges the C-rate ceiling for unrateable exits); no new kernel change is required by this family — the fail-closed band resolution (L-I3) raises BandResolutionError rather than defaulting

costs.charging: linear in fills (L-V14-0): fill_cost_bps = |dw| * band_bps * cost_mult / 10,000, charged exactly once per fill on traded notional, applied to booked PnL (never a sidecar); band from the trailing 63-session median dollar volume as of the decision (PIT); fail-closed band resolution (L-I3): a traded name without a computed band raises BandResolutionError — the silent 10 bps fallback is forbidden; exits of held names whose band has decayed to UNTRADABLE charge the conservative C-rate ceiling (resolve_exit_band_bps)
costs.stress: stress rerun at the stress bps above (20/30/50 per side = x2 base); stress must remain positive on PnL with PF >= 1.0
costs.turnover_ceiling: 6.0 two-way per year, annualized, raw and ceiling-normalized both reported

arms.role: causal/placebo control designed to refute the mechanism-specific explanation
arms.score: exposure = -first_lag_days of the most recent in-window filer-period, RAW and un-normalized (no own norm, no cohort norm, no scaling)
inputs: price series for inherited eligibility and fills only
arms.direction: low raw lag long, high raw lag short (same direction as the anchor for comparability)
arms.mechanism_refuted_if_reproduced: the mechanism claim is that the INCREMENTAL information is the per-filer norm-relative deviation: producing a filing materially later than one's own seasonal habit is firm-period-specific friction. If the raw un-normalized lag reproduces the anchor at >= 0.5x alpha ratio same-sign, the deseasonalization carries nothing — the effect is generic delay (a size/complexity/calendar-load proxy and the crude published anomaly), every convenient explanation survives, and the family dies as mechanism-mistitled
arms.differs_from_anchor_in_data_space: the control is the same lag variable BEFORE the own-history norm is subtracted; anchor and control share first_lag up to a per-filer affine transform, so their ranks are expected correlated (declared expectation rho 0.3-0.7, nonzero is legal) but must be < 0.95 (not rank-identical), measured at D2 pre-selection on the decision grid — the V4/V5 lesson (rho 0.78-0.83 caught pre-selection) is honored by measuring, never arguing

exposure_definition: Per entity e and decision session t on the inherited 21-session grid (PIT gate = 00:00 UTC of t; as-of: a group enters only at the first decision whose gate is strictly after its first_avail, never same-gate): (1) g*(e,t) = the filer-period group of e with the LARGEST first_avail(g) < gate(t) subject to gate(t) - first_avail(g) <= 800 days; if none, e abstains this decision. (2) z = own_z(g*) exactly as frozen in p0_v10_observable_manifest.json: [first_lag(g*) - median(first_lag over same-filer same-period-type prior groups with eff' < eff AND first_avail' <= first_avail(g*))] / (1.4826 * MAD of that sample), min_hist_own = 4; null rows (INSUFFICIENT_HISTORY, ZERO_SCALE) are excluded-with-reason and NEVER fall back to raw lag. (3) exposure(e,t) = -z. HIGHER exposure = negative own_z = filed EARLIER than own seasonal norm = LONG; LOWER exposure = positive own_z = later than own norm = SHORT. (4) Book: within the frozen sector tag, rank exposure-defined eligible names; long top tercile / short bottom tercile; equal weight; 0.5L/0.5S per active sector; CASH absorbs net; sectors with < 6 ranked names abstain; one-tercile retention hysteresis. D2 ranking contract: pooled Spearman rho of exposure(e,t) vs each of the nine veto entries computed on the SAME entity-decision pairs where the exposure is defined; pooled |rho| <= 0.20 required against all nine (63-session prior return, semivariance share, vol level, WC-stock intensity, Goodwill/Assets, F1 accrual flow, depletion-runway interaction, Cash/Assets, sector-exposure form).

margin_to_fail_expectations.falsification_fires_when: any inherited gate fails on the anchor, OR the raw-lag control reproduces >= 0.5x same-sign, OR the control outperforms a negative anchor, OR > 90% of short-leg expectancy comes from terminal-window exits, OR any D2 pre-selection screen is violated. Expected failure interpretation, preregistered: control-reproduction reject = 'the norm-relative construction carries no information beyond raw delay; the late-filer anomaly on this cohort is generic-delay form'; veto reject = 'timing ranks are a shadow of price-trend/cash characteristics on this cohort'; gate reject = 'disclosure-timeliness information does not survive band costs on the death-inclusive cohort' — each is a successful research outcome

literature: Givoly, D. and Palmon, D. (1982), 'Timeliness of Annual Earnings Announcements: Some Empirical Evidence', The Accounting Review 57(3) — late announcers' reports are systematically associated with poorer earnings news; lateness carries information.

Chambers, A.E. and Penman, S.H. (1984), 'Timeliness of Reporting and the Stock Price Reaction to Earnings Announcements', Journal of Accounting Research 22(1) — report lag negatively associated with announcement-window abnormal returns.

Kross, W. and Schroeder, D.A. (1984), 'An Empirical Investigation of the Effect of Quarterly Earnings Announcement Timing on Stock Returns', Journal of Accounting Research 22(1) — early announcers outperform late announcers; grounds the short-late/long-early direction.
Trueman, B. (1990), 'Theories of Earnings-Announcement Timing', The Accounting Review 65(2) — strategic delay of bad news; identifies the constrained actor (management) and the equilibrium incentive.
Begley, J. and Fischer, P.E. (1998), 'Is There Information in an Earnings Announcement Delay?', Review of Accounting Studies 3(3) — delays are informative about the sign and magnitude of news.

Bagnoli, M., Kross, W. and Watts, S.G. (2002), 'The Information in Managers' and Investors' Interim Financial Reports', The Accounting Review 77(Supplement) — reporting-timeliness quality is persistent per firm; grounds the own-history norm construction.

Sengupta, S. (2004), 'Disclosure Timing: Determinants of Quarterly Earnings Release Dates', Journal of Accounting and Public Policy 23(6) — release timing is a persistent firm policy tied to reporting infrastructure; grounds the seasonal-norm premise.

Doyle, J.T. and Magilke, M.J. (2009), 'The Timing of Earnings Announcements: Institutional and Aggregate Implications', The Accounting Review 84(2) — timing choice transmits information; markets partially read it.
McLean, R.D. and Pontiff, J. (2016), 'Does Academic Research Destroy Stock Return Predictability?', Journal of Finance 71(1) — post-publication decay caveat: a null result is a legitimate outcome.
